_meta.title: Kinematic-sequence / torque / GRF / X-factor reference v2 (open published sources only)
_meta.status: Published-only. Model-only above ~116 mph. Tags: fetched-full = full text/table read; abstract = abstract/landing page only; snippet = search-engine summary only (unverified); n/a = nothing found.

madrid2020.cite: Madrid, Avalos, Levine, Tuttle, Becker, Kwon. Appl Sci 10(17):5728 (2020), open access (CC BY)
madrid2020.note: Tables 1-4 read in full; 66 skilled males (hcp<=3), driver CHS 110.4+-4.8 mph, 500 Hz optical; on-plane (functional swing plane) angular velocities, not 3-axis resultant

meister2011.cite: Meister et al. J Appl Biomech 27:242-251 (2011)
meister2011.note: Full PDF text; 10 pro + 5 amateur males, 5-iron (not driver), easy/medium/hard effort; both feet on ONE force plate

bourgain2020.cite: Bourgain et al. Proceedings 49:45 (2020), open access
bourgain2020.note: Full text; 28 males, driver, best swing per golfer, Vicon 200 Hz + 2 AMTI plates (artificial turf), TrackMan CHS

okuda2010.cite: Okuda, Gribble, Armstrong. J Sports Sci Med 9:127-133 (2010), open access
okuda2010.note: Full PDF; 13 skilled vs 17 low-skilled, driver, vertical GRF only; CHS not reported

worsfold2007.cite: Worsfold, Smith, Dyson. golf shoe designs on natural turf, J Sports Sci Med (2007), PMC3794489
worsfold2007.note: PMC full page fetched; 24 golfers, natural-turf force plates; CHS not reported in the numbers used

worsfold2008.cite: Worsfold, Smith, Dyson. rotational torque at shoe-turf interface, PMC3761900
worsfold2008.note: PMC full page fetched; 24 golfers (8 low/8 mid/8 high hcp), natural turf, 5 shots per club; CHS not reported

foxworth2013.cite: Foxworth et al. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 43(9):660-665 (2013)
foxworth2013.note: Full article page incl. Table 1-3; torques normalised to % body weight x height; absolute N*m needs assumed anthropometry

okamoto2006.cite: Okamoto. ISBS proceedings, joint torque contribution to clubhead acceleration (case study)
okamoto2006.note: Full paper; 3 professionals (63.3 kg, 1.70 m), 250 Hz Vicon, fastest of 5 drives; club-grip (hand-club) torque and power, not body-joint torque

sprigings2000.cite: Sprigings & Neal. J Appl Biomech 16:356-366 (2000), simulation
sprigings2000.note: Scanned PDF (no text layer); pages 3,5,6 read as images. SIMULATION: torque limits are model inputs, torque histories are optimiser outputs read from a figure (+-5 N*m)

lynn2013.cite: Lynn et al. Int J Golf Sci 2:116-125 (2013), open access
lynn2013.note: Full PDF; 5-iron; 15 elite vs 14 recreational; electromagnetic/optical pelvis plate; FlightScope

callaway2012.cite: Callaway et al. peak pelvis rotation speed and gluteal strength, PMC3362989
callaway2012.note: PMC page; 56 subjects incl. tour players, 7/8-iron, K-Vest; CHS not reported

chu2010.cite: Chu, Sell, Lephart. J Sports Sci 28:1251-1259 (2010)
chu2010.note: Full PDF (course handout copy); 308 golfers (266 M / 42 F, hcp 8.4+-8.4), driver; values are at swing EVENTS, not peaks; CHS not measured (ball velocity 61.0+-8.7 m/s = 136.5 mph)

ichikawa2024.cite: Ichikawa et al. J Hum Sport Exerc 19(3):874-881 (2024), open access CC BY-NC-SA
ichikawa2024.note: Full PDF; ONE long-drive professional (182.5 cm, 106 kg, 27 y), GEARS 360 fps, GC2 launch monitor, 30 drives; 'kinematic sequence (deg/sec)' values are reported near impact, peak-vs-at-impact not stated

randa_wld2019.cite: R&A / Nov 2019: Analysis of TrackMan data gathered at World Long Drive events (v1.0)
randa_wld2019.note: Launch-monitor population data only (no biomechanics); defines the >140 mph population that has no joint data

watson2026.cite: Watson et al. Sports Med 56(5):1191-1212 (2026), systematic review of GRF/CoP in golf, open access
watson2026.note: Full HTML; summary tables of primary studies (secondary values for Han 2019, Ball & Best, Williams, Bourgain, Peterson); no N*m or CHS-by-group numbers

horan2012.note: Abstract fetched; peak-speed numbers (650/507 deg/s, CHS 50.1 m/s) came from a search-engine summary only

han2019_ground.cite: Han, Como, Kim, Lee, Kim, Kim, Kwon. Sports Biomech 18:115-134 (2019)
han2019_ground.note: Paywalled; abstract only. Correlation values via Watson 2026 (fetched-full secondary). No N*m or BW means retrieved

han2019_style.cite: Han, Como, Kim, Hung, Hasan, Kwon. Sports Biomech 18:663-685 (2019)
han2019_style.note: Paywalled; abstract summary only; phase-time means by swing style taken from Madrid 2020 text (secondary)

kwon2013.cite: Kwon, Han, Como, Lee, Singhal. Sports Biomech 12:231-246 (2013)
kwon2013.note: Abstract + docksci first page; 18 skilled males, 5 driver trials; X-factor values via Madrid 2020 (secondary); CHS from a slide-deck snippet

healy2011.cite: Healy, Moran, Dickson, et al. J Sports Sci 29:1005-1015 (2011)
healy2011.note: Repository abstract; 5-iron, 30 males split by ball speed 52.9 vs 39.9 m/s; no body-segment peaks retrieved

lumbar_loads.cite: Lumbar spinal loads during a golf swing (EMG-assisted model); thesis/paper summaries
lumbar_loads.note: Search-engine summary only (about 6 BW / 4300 N compression near driver impact; AP shear 882 N); attribution between the thesis and a Sports Biomech paper unresolved; forces, not torque

sonic_arxiv.cite: The Physics behind the Sonic Golf Swing Monitoring Device (arXiv 1001.1137)

conflicts.C1: Pelvis peak speed vs CHS: Madrid (driver, n=66) r=0.447 for the hip line, but Lynn (5-iron, n=29) r=0.017 and elite/recreational peaks 428/399 deg/s; tour/skilled group means cluster at 428-507 deg/s (Lynn 428, Parker 475 [v1], Cheetham 477 [v1], Horan 507 snippet, Callaway 503) with no consistent rise from 92 to 112 mph. Treat the v1 pelvis speed extrapolation (519 at 120, 565 at 132) as an UPPER bound.
conflicts.C2: The only long-drive datum (one 137 mph player, n=1) shows pelvis 284-325, torso 610-650 and arm 460-480 deg/s near impact: not above 110 mph skilled values (Madrid hip line 394, shoulder line 711). Definition mismatch (peak vs at-impact, GEARS vs Kwon3D) prevents a direct subtraction, but there is no evidence that body-segment speeds keep rising to 132 mph. v1 segment extrapolations (pelvis 565, thorax 886, arm 1226 at 132) are unsupported upper bounds; club speed may come from a longer/lower-loft club, mass (106 kg), lever/grip release.
conflicts.C3: Horizontal GRF: Bourgain max 0.13-0.19 BW per foot (resultant, 28 golfers) vs v1 review's 0.4-0.6 BW AP shear (Hume review) and Worsfold AP range 0.31-0.34 BW (irons). Different definitions (per-foot vs summed vs range). No resolution.
conflicts.C4: Lead-foot peak vertical GRF: lab plates 1.09-1.24 BW (Okuda 1.09 skilled, Bourgain 1.18 pros/1.24 amateurs; v1 Han snippet 1.12) vs natural turf 0.84 BW (Worsfold, driver). Surface and shoe, not skill, probably explain it.
conflicts.C5: Vertical-axis moment: Meister free moment 1.19 N*m/kg (about 99 N*m for 83 kg; 5-iron, hard, both feet on one plate) vs Worsfold foot torsional Tz 17-19 (front) + 6-7 (back) N*m on turf (driver) vs v1's Barrentine 17-26 N*m per foot. They measure different things (free moment about the combined CoP includes the couple of horizontal forces; foot Tz is torsional only). Do not use Worsfold Tz as the pelvis-yaw requirement.
conflicts.C6: X-factor at impact: Madrid 9+-8 deg (FSP-based) vs Meister 33+-6 (hard 5-iron pros) vs Kwon: conventional horizontal-plane method gives substantially larger X-factor than FSP/Cardan methods. Top-of-backswing X-factor agrees better (Madrid 61, Meister 56, Parker 54.9, Chu 49 heterogeneous).
conflicts.C7: Club-grip torque: Okamoto measured 40.9 N*m at 102.4 mph (n=3) vs the v1 linear fit through Nesbit's four swings (29 N*m at 100 mph, 45 at 120). Club peak power: Okamoto 2813 W at 102.4 mph vs v1 power-law about 2.2-2.4 kW at 100-102 mph. v1 under-predicts grip torque by ~30% and club peak power by ~15-20% at ~102 mph (n=3).
conflicts.C8: Downswing duration: Sprigings simulation 380 ms vs measured professional 250-280 ms (Madrid, Bourgain, Okamoto, Sonic 258 ms snippet). Do not use the simulation timing.
conflicts.C9: Hip axial torque: Foxworth peaks (internal rotators 2.70 + 3.21 % BW*Ht, about 87 N*m for both hips at the assumed 83 kg/1.80 m, amateurs at ~92 mph) vs v1's ~290 N*m 'average hip torque' derived from Nesbit hip WORK (flexion/extension dominated). The v1 number is an energy-equivalent, not an axial pelvis-turning torque.
conflicts.C10: X-factor stretch: skilled joint-coordinate/FSP studies 1-6 deg (Madrid, Kwon, Parker) vs Cheetham 2001 sensor method ~19% (v1). Keep stretch as a small additive.

remaining_gaps: No peak lumbar/trunk-axial or shoulder torque in N*m measured in a real swing was found in an open source (only Sprigings model torques and Foxworth hips in % BW*Ht).

No joint-level biomechanics (peak speeds by segment, timing, GRF, X-factor) for a population above ~112 mph (n=14, snippet) apart from ONE 137 mph long-drive player's near-impact body speeds (Ichikawa 2024). No GRF at any speed above ~118 mph.

Han 2019 GRF means (BW and N*m for the 63 skilled golfers), Kwon 2013 / Han 2019 style tables, Hellstrom 2009, Ball & Best primary, Wallace/Koenig/Mann, Ae, Lynn GRF, Healy segment peaks, Sasaki, Brown 2011 (female) remain abstract-level or not retrieved (paywalled).
Horan & Kavanagh 2012 peak speeds (thorax 650, pelvis 507, CHS 50.1 m/s) are snippet-level; a full-text read is needed before use.
Madrid on-plane speeds are not the same definition as Cheetham's 3-axis resultant speeds; a common-definition conversion was not found.
Dependence of peak torque/power on CHS above 52 m/s (116 mph) is still extrapolation; torque-vs-CHS scaling exponents are assumptions.
